annotationRationale: Valid sequences correspond uniquely to choices of gaps containing two ones. Combinations count these choices, and the addition principle combines the disjoint cases for the number of zeros.
sourceMethod: Followed the official alternative that classifies sequences by their number of zeros, adding explicit bounds and a one-to-one correspondence to justify completeness and lack of duplicates.

review.mathCheck: With \(k\) zeros, the \(k-1\) internal gaps each contain one or two ones. Thus \(k-1\le19-k\le2(k-1)\), giving exactly \(k=7,8,9,10\). Choosing the \(20-2k\) doubled gaps yields counts \(1,35,28,1\), totaling \(65\), choice C. The encoding is reversible, and the cases are exhaustive and disjoint.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA AMC 10B solution 25's second approach, page 13. The candidate derives the official four zero-count cases uniformly and explicitly explains why choosing doubled gaps counts each valid sequence once.
review.annotationCheck: The direct nodes and assessed/support roles match the chosen method. Bijective encoding and combinations are assessed; addition combines the disjoint cases. A recurrence node is unnecessary.
